# Codex pull request naming rules

When Codex opens or updates a pull request, the PR title must follow Conventional Commits:

- Format: `<type>(optional-scope): short description`
- Allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `update`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`
- Keep the title concise and descriptive (CI enforces that the description portion — the text after `: ` — is 1–100 characters long; the `type`/optional scope/`!` prefix is not counted)
- **CI enforcement**: The commit-lint workflow will **reject** PR titles from Codex that contain:
  - Generic terms: `Codex`, `Copilot`, `AI`, `autogenerated`, `bot`, `automation`
  - Vague descriptions: `update code`, `fix issue`, `apply changes`, `make changes`, or standalone words like `update`, `fix`, `change`

Good examples:
- `feat(kernel): add zenpower module installation`
- `fix(installer): guard missing portage set directories`
- `ci(commit-lint): reject non-conventional PR titles`
- `docs: add ROCm installation prerequisites`

Bad examples (will be rejected by CI):
- `fix: Codex-generated pull request`
- `feat: AI-generated changes`
- `update: fix issue`
- `docs: update`
